records.people: Ahmed Ghaleb Al-Maabaqi (أحمد غالب المعبقي), appointed Governor of the Central Bank of Yemen by presidential decree of President Abdrabbuh Mansour Hadi, reported by Al Arabiya on 7 December 2021; Mohammed Omar Banajah was named Deputy Governor in the same decree
records.move: from Director of the Financial Planning Department (1985-1987), Director General of External Financial Relations (1987-1995) and Undersecretary for External Financial Relations (1995-2005) at Yemen's Ministry of Finance, then Deputy Head (2005-2007) and Head (2007 to June 2014) of the Tax Authority, and chairman of the board of the General Holding Corporation for Real Estate Development and Investment immediately before appointment, to Governor of the Central Bank of Yemen
records.summary: Al Arabiya's profile of the incoming Central Bank of Yemen governor publishes his dated career list, and every employer in it is a public body: Yemen's Ministry of Finance from 1985 to 2005, the Tax Authority from 2005 to June 2014, two terms on the executive board of the Arab Monetary Fund in Abu Dhabi (1996-2002 and 2007-2010), and the chairmanship of the state General Holding Corporation for Real Estate Development and Investment, which the article says he held immediately before the decree. No commercial or private bank appears anywhere in the list, so the record is filed as a public move and no ownership question arises.
records.detail: This is the first career record of any kind for Yemen on this row; round 68 read four Yemeni career lists (the National Bank of Yemen's own CV board, an AGSI profile of deputy governor Mansour Rageh, Wikipedia on the governor and an Arab Planning Institute expert CV) and recorded that none of them gave a dated career for the sitting governor. The Al Arabiya profile, published the day after the decree reconstituting the central bank's board, supplies that dated career, and it runs entirely through the finance ministry, the tax authority, the Arab Monetary Fund and a state holding corporation. The deputy governor named in the same decree, Mohammed Omar Banajah, is given no career by the article.

records.people: Sereana Moira Marum (Reserve Bank of Vanuatu from May 2006 for sixteen years, rising from Settlement Officer to Director of Support Services; director of the National Bank of Vanuatu board from February 2023 and Chairlady of that board from October 2024)
records.move: from trainee accountant at Equity Investment Group (2003) to the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu in May 2006, rising to Director of Support Services over sixteen years; then out of the central bank in 2022 to the Vanuatu-Australia Health Partnership, and onto the board of the National Bank of Vanuatu from February 2023 as the director representing the Vanuatu National Provident Fund, becoming board Chairlady in October 2024
records.summary: The Sista profile gives a full dated career for a Reserve Bank of Vanuatu director: a first job in 2003 as trainee accountant at Equity Investment Group, sixteen years inside the Reserve Bank from May 2006 ending as Director of Support Services, a move in 2022 to the donor-funded Vanuatu-Australia Health Partnership, and from February 2023 a seat on the National Bank of Vanuatu board held as the representative of the Vanuatu National Provident Fund, with the chairship from October 2024. The page states no ownership for Equity Investment Group and describes the National Bank of Vanuatu only as a national bank, and the seat itself is held for a statutory provident fund, so the move is filed as public.
records.detail: Round 68 read the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu's own career lists to the end and found every career in them public; this record comes from the hiring side rather than the bank's own pages, which is the route that was left unopened. The one employer whose character could have moved the row, Equity Investment Group, is named by the page as the site of a 2003 traineeship with no description of its business and no statement of its ownership, so it cannot be counted; and the National Bank of Vanuatu seat is expressly held on behalf of the Vanuatu National Provident Fund, a statutory fund. The record is therefore a filled box rather than a counted move.

records.summary: Round 68 established that the Banco Central de Timor-Leste publishes a name, a title and a photograph for each of its seven board members and not one line of career, so the only career available for deputy governor Sara Lobo Brites comes from outside the bank. The Wikipedia entry gives two posts and no dates beyond the five-year length of the central bank term: Vice-Governor of the central bank, and afterwards Deputy Minister of Finance in the VIII Constitutional Government. Both are public posts and no private bank, insurer or asset manager appears, so the record is filed as a public move; it rests on an encyclopaedia entry rather than a primary document.
records.detail: This fills the second of the two named deputy-governor gaps left open for Timor-Leste last round. It is filed with a weak source because the only page found that states her career at all is the Wikipedia entry; the Timorese government's own tomada de posse release for the governor is published as a PDF but no equivalent release for either deputy governor surfaced in search. The other named deputy governor, Rafael Borges, still has no career on any page reached, and the privately owned banks licensed in Timor-Leste remain the route that would be needed to move this row rather than fill it.

blanks.note: MRT: the Mauritanian private-bank route named as the next step last round was opened on two banks and neither publishes a career that touches the Banque Centrale de Mauritanie. (1) Forbes Afrique's profile of Banque El Amana, https://forbesafrique.com/mauritanie-la-bea-simpose-comme-reference-de-la-finance-de-proximite/, read in full: it names exactly one executive, Mohamed Ahmed Salem Bouna Moctar, Director General of BEA and president of the Federation des institutions financieres de Mauritanie, and gives his whole career - mathematics at the Universite de Tours, a master's in financial engineering at ESSCA Paris, BNP Paribas in Paris, then BEA from 2003 in documentary credit, rising to directeur de l'exploitation and directeur general adjoint. No central bank post at any point; the article mentions the BCM only as having designated BEA a market maker. It also states nothing whatever about BEA's ownership or shareholders, naming IFC, KfW and Proparco only as financing partners. The photo caption refers to a 'Comite Executif' and lists no names. (2) Financial Afrik's report on the Nouvelle Banque de Mauritanie board, https://www.financialafrik.com/2020/08/11/la-nouvelle-banque-de-mauritanie-nbm-nomme-ses-nouveaux-administrateurs, read in full: four administrators named - James Clayton (president of the conseil d'administration, also president of WMR), JD Diabira (directeur general of Westbridge Mortgage REIT), Jacques Raiche and Maitre Sylvere Koyo - with no prior employer and no date for any of the four, no mention of the central bank, and no shareholder detail beyond the phrase 'recomposition de l'actionnariat de la banque'. (3) Financial Afrik's 2016 profile of the financier Mory Gueta Cisse, https://financialafrik.com/2016/03/12/mory-gueta-cisse-le-retour-glorieux-dun-financier-par-vocation, read to 100,000 of its 108,725 characters: he was administrateur-directeur delegue of BMCI in Mauritania and directeur general of the International Bank for Commerce in Banjul and of Sunbeach Hotel in Gambia, but the article says he never worked at the BCM, and it states no ownership for BMCI beyond saying that BMCI's own leaders bought out the state's and the Egyptian partner AAIB's shares. Not reached: Attijari Bank Mauritanie's and Banque Internationale d'Investissement's own governance pages, neither of which surfaced as a board page in two French-language searches.

TON: the non-executive directors of the National Reserve Bank of Tonga board were again not reached, and the reason is now documented rather than a budget shortfall. Two searches aimed squarely at the annual report's governance section - one for the NRBT annual report board of directors, one restricted to reservebank.to - returned no annual report PDF from the bank's own domain at all; what they returned was Centralbanking.com's paywalled record of the 2006/07 and 2007/08 annual reports, IMF Article IV staff reports, Matangi Tonga tag listings, and Wikipedia mirrors. The one Matangi Tonga page opened this round, https://matangitonga.to/node/40526, turns out to be a job advertisement for a Central Banking Governance Adviser post funded by Australia's DFAT under the Tonga Australia Support Platform; it discusses the NRBT Board Rules 2021 and the Board Audit and Risk Committee Charter and names no director. So the governor and deputy-governor line is exhausted (round 68) and the non-executive line is still untested. What I would open next: the NRBT annual report is tabled in the Legislative Assembly, so the Tongan parliament's own tabled-papers listing, or the Pacific gazette mirror rms.paclii.org/to/other/TOGovGaz/ which search did surface for Tonga, is the way to a board list that reservebank.to is not serving to search engines.

TLS: one of the two named deputy governors is now filed (Sara Lobo Brites, central bank then Deputy Minister of Finance, both public, on a Wikipedia entry) and the other is a confirmed blank. A search pairing both names with the bank, 'vice-governador' and 'tomada de posse' returned, for Rafael Borges, nothing at all: no government swearing-in release, no news profile, no page of any kind giving him a career. The hits were the Wikipedia entry for Lobo Brites and its mirrors, the customs.gov.tl enquiry-point page on who the Vice-Minister of Finance is, the governor's own 2023 tomada de posse PDF already used for the Helder Lopes record, and unrelated Rui Gomes swearing-in releases. Combined with round 68's finding that bancocentral.tl publishes name, title and photograph for all seven board members under a heading still reading 'Add board members here', the central bank side of Timor-Leste is now worked out. The only route that could move rather than fill this row is the privately owned banks licensed in Timor-Leste - the Australian and Indonesian banks' local branches - since BNCTL is state-owned; none of their board pages surfaced in this round's search.

STP: Sao Tome and Principe has now actually been tested, which it had not been. Forbes Africa Lusofona's report of the appointment, 'Banco Central de Sao Tome e Principe tem novo governador', https://forbesafricalusofona.com/?p=50560, was opened and read: it names Americo d'Oliveira dos Ramos as replacing Americo Soares de Barros and gives his career in a single clause, 'foi ministro das Financas do Governo de Patrice Trovoada entre 2014 e 2018', plus a non-employment note that he was detained for about three months in 2019 on charges prosecutors dropped that July. It names no commercial or private bank, and states no bank's ownership. That is the same single public post the existing map record already carries, so the article adds a second source for it and no new career. The Portuguese-language search that found it returned no Sao Tomean document carrying a CV for anyone else: the other hits were the Wikipedia entry on the central bank and its IPFS mirrors, Centralbanking.com's paywalled items on the 2022 dismissal and the 2026 appointment, the Forbes articles on the exoneration, Caixa Geral de Depositos' historical page on the BNU branch, and the bank's own Plano Estrategico 2021-2024 and governor's speech PDFs. Still unopened: the Plano Estrategico, and the Assembleia Nacional diaries mirrored at www2.camara.leg.br/saotomeeprincipe (DAN21-IIS.pdf), which record the parliamentary hearings on central bank appointments. The employer that would have to be settled for a conversion remains Afriland First Bank STP or Ecobank STP, since BISTP is split between the Sao Tomean state and Caixa Geral de Depositos and both are public.

DJI: the first of the three Djiboutian commercial banks named as the remaining route was opened and it carries no careers. Bank of Africa Mer Rouge's financial statements for 2022, https://www.boamerrouge.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/EF-DJ_2022_VF-Web.pdf, were downloaded and extracted; the section 'Conseil d'administration au 31/12/2022' names four directors - Abderrazzak Zebdani (President), Amine Bouabid (representant de BOA GROUP S.A.), Abdelali Nadifi and Farid Bouri - with a title each and not one line of career, and no mention anywhere in the document of the Banque Centrale de Djibouti except a solvency ratio against its regulatory norm. The document has a heading 'Actionnariat au 31/12/2022' whose content does not extract, so the shareholding is published as an image and was not read; the capital is given as 1.5 billion Djiboutian francs. Note that this host publishes the same thin statement-of-accounts format for every year from 2011 to 2022, so the other years will not carry careers either. With round 68's finding that the central bank's own Rapport Annuel 2024 names nobody but Governor Ahmed Osman and gives him no career, Djibouti now has two documents read and no career anywhere. Not reached: the board or management pages of Bank Salaam African Bank (banksalaam.com) and BCIMR, the two remaining banks on the list.

YEM: the Arabic private-bank route named as the remaining lead could not be opened, and the Arabic search that was supposed to reach it failed. A search in Arabic for the board of directors of Tadhamon Bank with CVs and the Central Bank of Yemen returned no board page for Tadhamon, the International Bank of Yemen, Yemen Kuwait Bank or Saba Islamic Bank; the hits were two PDFs on the central bank's own site cby-ye.com, the Yemen banking governance code of 2013 on ecgi.global, an Al-Ayyam news item, a Scribd upload of guidelines for government banks, Centralbanking.com's paywalled report of a governor's dismissal, and a Devex organisation page. So the Yemeni private banks' own board pages are still unopened, not because they were skipped but because neither an Arabic nor an English search surfaced one. What did convert is the other half of the brief's advice, searching for the person rather than the page: Al Arabiya's 7 December 2021 profile of the incoming governor publishes a twelve-entry dated career and it is filed as this round's Yemen record, all of it public. The record is the first of any kind for Yemen on this row. Next step for a conversion rather than a fill: the banks' own domains tadhamonbank.com and ibyemen.com approached directly for a 'مجلس الإدارة' page, since search is not indexing them.

BTN: both untested Bhutanese routes were tested and neither publishes a biography. (1) Druk PNB Bank's own board and management page, https://drukpnbbank.bt/about-us/bod-management-team/, read in full: it carries no career history of any kind, only names, roles and departments for seven directors - Aum Sangay Om (Chairperson), K.V. Satyanarayana and Sonam Tshering Dorji (Independent Directors), Pawan Singh and Sumesh Kumar (PNB Nominee Directors), Ugyen Namgyel (Public Shareholder Director) and K. Meera Bai (CEO) - and thirteen management staff. No one on the page states any Royal Monetary Authority service, and the page states no shareholding percentage for Punjab National Bank, no private Bhutanese holding and no listing; the only ownership signals are the two director designations themselves. (2) Bhutan National Bank's Annual Report 2024, https://bnb.bt/wp-content/uploads/dld/ANNUAL%20REPORTS/Year%202024/BNB_AR_2024%20Final.pdf, downloaded and fully extracted (382,404 characters) and grepped for 'Royal Monetary Authority', 'RMA', 'sharehold' and 'promoter': the Board of Directors page gives five names with titles only - Dasho Karma Tshiteem (Chairperson), Dago Beda, Namgay Tenzin, Sonam Tobgay (DHI) and Sonam Tobgay (CEO) - with no biography; every one of the thirty-odd RMA matches in the document is a regulatory or settlement-account reference, not a career; and there is no shareholding-pattern table at all, the hits for NPPF, RGoB and Royal Insurance Corporation being entries in the abbreviations list and in the interbank-balances notes. The one lead this leaves is a separately published bio PDF for the BNB chairperson, 'Dasho_Karma_Tshiteem_bio__SLS.pdf' on gevme.com, which search surfaced and which was not opened for budget; even if it showed RMA service it could only be filed as a public move, because neither Bhutanese bank states its ownership on any page reached. With round 68's eight individual CV PDFs on the FITI site worked to the end, Bhutan is now a thoroughly documented blank.

VUT: the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu Annual Report 2024, https://rbv.gov.vu/images/Annual_Reports/2024/Final%20ANNUAL%20REPORT%202024%2007%20Nov.pdf, does carry board biographies - the first Vanuatu document found that does - and not one of the five board members has ever worked at a commercial bank, an insurer or any other private financial firm. Andrew Kausiama (Chairman) is a former RBV Governor 1998-2003 whose other posts are the Prime Minister's Office, the Ministries of Trade and Finance, research at the RBV and development planning at USP. August Letlet (Governor, ex officio) comes from senior roles at the Ministry of Finance and Economic Management and chairs the Vanuatu National Provident Fund, which the report itself describes as the statutory sole mandatory superannuation fund. Serah Obed spent nineteen years to 2019 as Deputy Commissioner of the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission, a government regulator, after senior and principal auditor posts at the Auditor General's Office. Two directors have private employers that are not financial and are therefore logged here rather than filed: Stephen Tahi, fourteen years at the Ministry of Lands then a fifteen-year private consultancy practice and a recognised associate of a local law firm; and Votausi Lucy-Ann Mackenzie-Reur, who runs Lapita Cafe and Lapita Lodge and is a director of Fibreglass Vanuatu Limited and Pacific Polytanks Limited, after teaching at Malapoa College and serving as National Nutrition Coordinator at the Department of Health. Note that curl cannot reach rbv.gov.vu at all - it fails certificate verification twice, including with the agent CA bundle - and WebFetch served the PDF without trouble, so use WebFetch for this host. Not reached: BRED Bank Vanuatu's and ANZ Vanuatu's own board pages, neither of which surfaced in the search; the National Bank of Vanuatu's annual reports for 2024 and 2025 are published on nbv.vu and were not opened, and they are where a fuller biography of the NBV board, including this round's record, would sit.

checked_not_in_assignment.note: Fiji occurred to me while reading the Pacific search results - the Reserve Bank of Fiji page rbf.gov.fj was returned by the Tonga search and the Vanuatu careers run through Fijian institutions. Looked it up in have_rd.json first as the common brief requires: FJI is present in that file, so it is already on this row and nothing was filed for it. Nothing fetched for it either.

Bank of Bhutan's own annual reports on bob.bt (2012-2024) were returned repeatedly by the Bhutan search and were deliberately not opened: Bank of Bhutan is the employer already carried by the existing Damche Tenzin record for BTN, so a board list there would duplicate rather than add, and Bhutan is in my assignment so this is not an out-of-assignment country, only a declined duplicate route.

leads_not_opened.note: The Tongan Legislative Assembly's own tabled-papers listing, and the Pacific gazette mirror rms.paclii.org/to/other/TOGovGaz/, as the way to an NRBT board list. Neither the bank's annual report nor any board-profile page is being served to search engines from reservebank.to, so the parliamentary and gazette routes are the ones left. Ownership of any private employer found would then still have to be settled separately, most plausibly through BSP Financial Group's Port Moresby listing.

tadhamonbank.com and ibyemen.com approached directly for a board-of-directors page in Arabic, since neither an Arabic nor an English search indexes them; also Yemen Kuwait Bank and Saba Islamic Bank. This is the only route left that could move Yemen rather than fill it.

Bank Salaam African Bank (banksalaam.com) and BCIMR board or management pages - the last two Djiboutian banks on the list. BOA Mer Rouge is now closed: its statements name four directors with no careers and publish the shareholding only as an image.

The BNB chairperson's separately published bio PDF, Dasho_Karma_Tshiteem_bio__SLS.pdf on gevme.com, which would at best give a public move since neither Bhutanese bank states its ownership on any reached page; and the Royal Monetary Authority's own annual report management profiles, which were not found as a PDF in this round's search (only a 2002/03 RMA annual report mirrored on apfanews.com surfaced).

National Bank of Vanuatu annual reports on nbv.vu (NBV AR 2024 - FINAL.pdf and AR_2025.pdf, both returned by search), which would carry a fuller biography of the NBV board including this round's record, and BRED Bank Vanuatu's board page. Use WebFetch and not curl for rbv.gov.vu.

The Assembleia Nacional diaries mirrored at www2.camara.leg.br/saotomeeprincipe (DAN21-IIS.pdf), which record parliamentary hearings on central bank appointments, and the BCSTP's own Plano_Estrategico_bcstp_2021_2024.pdf. For a conversion rather than a fill, Afriland First Bank's or Ecobank's group structure page stating the Sao Tomean subsidiary's shareholding.

Attijari Bank Mauritanie's and Banque Internationale d'Investissement's own governance pages; neither surfaced as a board page in two French-language searches, so they would have to be approached on their own domains. Also the Financial Afrik interview with BII's Nicolas Roca (13 May 2026), which was returned twice and not opened - a serving private-bank director general, so a central bank career in him would be the one Mauritanian document that settles career and employer together.

The board pages of the Australian and Indonesian banks' branches licensed in Timor-Leste, as the only non-state banking employers there; BNCTL is state-owned and cannot convert. No such page surfaced in this round's search.
